parallel.requirements: Recognized the required Node.js ESM migration, .mjs suffixes, manual command-line parsing, no external dependencies, schedule job repr/state behavior, and output parity against the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although the run started with swarm mode enabled, the main agent explicitly kept ownership because the task was small and tightly coupled; no child, handoff, join, or multi-agent work unit was created.
parallel.implementation: The main agent observed executable behavior, created /output/lib/errors.mjs, /output/lib/job.mjs, /output/lib/scheduler.mjs, /output/lib/argparse.mjs, and /output/test10.mjs, then patched argparse abbreviation and -h handling.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The implementation was assembled directly in /output with an entry file and local .mjs imports; artifact validation later listed test10.mjs and four library files as accepted deliverables.
parallel.verification: The run compared happy paths, invalid times, duplicate args, equals-form args, missing args, unknown args, and help variants; it treated the remaining help prog-name difference as expected and official evaluation passed 150/150.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished behavior remains; the only self-noted local diffs were help prog-name differences from script basename behavior, and no child work was left unjoined.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual argparse, no external dependency, schedule behavior, and /output deliverable requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial control used one main agent throughout, with no delegation; the agent kept probing, implementation, integration, and verification under the same owner.
serial.implementation: The main agent created lib/argparse.mjs, lib/job.mjs, lib/scheduler.mjs, and test10.mjs, then refined time validation, exact ScheduleValueError messages, traceback line selection, and stdout buffering.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The implementation was assembled directly in /output with a test10.mjs entry file and local library imports; artifact validation listed the entry and three library files as accepted deliverables.
serial.verification: The serial run checked help and argument errors, a wide set of valid and invalid --a time values, output/stderr ordering, exit codes, and ended with a final ALL MATCH comparison before official 150/150 pass.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished behavior remains; earlier diffs in invalid-time ordering were fixed before closure, and the final local matrix plus evaluator both succeeded.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in 451.381 agent seconds, with no timeout and no provider retry; it closed after direct implementation and local tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 1386.742 agent seconds, with no timeout and no provider retry; it spent more time refining edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was shorter, serial was longer, and neither run exhausted budget or left required work unfinished.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial passed 150 of 150 samples. The task-solving difference is that parallel-mode execution entered swarm mode but did not actually delegate, then completed a direct implementation faster, while serial performed a longer single-agent refinement loop and final all-match matrix. Because no child or multi-agent mechanism executed in the parallel run, there is no retained concurrency-error pattern.
parallel_contributors: Single main actor directly implemented the scheduler, argparse, and entry modules.
Local behavioral probes and final official evaluation were sufficient for a full pass.
serial_contributors: Single main actor performed broader local edge-case verification and fixed stdout/stderr ordering.
Final local matrix and official evaluation both confirmed full pass.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel split ScheduleValueError into a separate errors module; serial kept it in job.mjs.
Serial explicitly buffered stdout for invalid-time stderr ordering, while parallel treated PyInstaller/runtime-specific output differences as outside required stdout parity.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process differences do not create a concurrency failure
